description: Mutation testing for Kotlin via a K2 compiler plugin. Mutations are injected at compile time into a test-only compilation, so they run inside your normal test suite and production JARs stay clean.
rules: Start from the mutflow Agent Guide (docs/agent-guide.md): a task-oriented reference with a copy-pasteable snippet per task - setup, targets, mutation tests, CI phases, timeouts, traps, suppression and common mistakes.
Apply the Gradle plugin `id("io.github.anschnapp.mutflow")`. It adds the mutflow-core and mutflow-junit6 dependencies automatically - never declare them by hand.
Match the mutflow release to the project's Kotlin version: mutflow 1.1.0+ needs Kotlin 2.4.x, mutflow up to 1.0.3 needs Kotlin 2.2.x-2.3.x. A mismatch fails with an obscure compiler error.
Choose what gets mutated with the `@MutationTarget` annotation on the class, or with `mutflow { targets = listOf("com.example.service.**") }` in build.gradle.kts. Both can be combined.
Write mutation tests as normal JUnit 6 tests annotated with `@MutFlowTest`, and wrap the exercised code in `MutFlow.underTest { }`. Mutations are inactive outside that block.
Mutation testing runs inside the normal `./gradlew test` run - there is no separate mutation task. Never add one.
For phased CI, set the `MUTFLOW_VERIFICATION_MODE` env var to DISABLED (fast feedback), LENIENT (report survivors only) or STRICT (default, survivors fail the build).
Green mutation runs are expected: a killed mutation swallows the assertion error and reports PASSED. Read the printed summary and the build status, not the individual test results.
A surviving mutation means a missing assertion. Fix the test instead of suppressing it; `@SuppressMutations` and `// mutflow:ignore` are for equivalent mutants and code not worth testing.
Set `mutflow { enabled = false }` or `-Pmutflow.enabled=false` to disable mutation testing with zero build overhead. Use this for JaCoCo/Kover runs, which report 0% while mutations are active.
Do not add manual guards to strip mutations from release builds. Mutations only ever land in the separate `mutatedMain` compilation, so production JARs are clean by construction.
